newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Bhutto says not afraid of arrest in murder case.
newsitem.headline: Bhutto says not afraid of arrest in murder case.

text.p: Former Pakistani prime minister Benazir Bhutto said on Tuesday she was not afraid of being arrested in what she called a baseless case of murder registered against her last week while she was abroad.
"I am not afraid of arrest and jail," she told reporters on return home after a week's private visit to Britain.
Bhutto and two of her aides were accused of responsibility in the killings of two members of the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM) in Karachi in December 1995 in the case registered on April 9.

The complaint in the so-called first information report was made by Sindh province Labour Minister Shoaib Bukhari, who is also a member of the MQM, an ally of Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League (PML) party.

The registration of the case brought protests from Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party (PPP) and charges of blackmail by Sharif's government, which told parliament that it was not involved in the complaint.
More than 2,000 PPP followers chanted welcoming slogans as Bhutto emerged from Karachi airport.
"This is absolutely baseless allegation," Bhutto said of the murder complaint, which police said last week would be investigated by a special team of officials.

Bhutto, whose three-year-old government was sacked by President Farooq Leghari in November on disputed charges of misrule and whose party was defeated in the February 3 elections, said the case was registered to pressurise her to leave Pakistan and live abroad in exile.
"I want to live in Pakistan. I will face it for the sake of the people of Pakistan," she added.

Bukhari's report said Arif Hussain and Nasir Hussain, close relatives of MQM founder Altaf Hussain, were kidnapped from their homes and their bullet-riddled bodies were recovered from an outskirt of Karachi on December 12, 1995, when violence was at its climax in the industrial port city.
More more than 2,000 people were killed in ethnic, sectarian and political violence in Karachi in 1995.

Bhutto's estranged brother Murtaza was killed near his home in Karachi last September and his breakaway PPP group accuses Bhutto's jailed husband Asif Ali Zardari of conspiring its leader's murder of Murtaza. Zardari denies the charge.
